📌 Flash Loans: Borrowing Without Collateral for One Transaction

Main Points
⏺ A flash loan lets you borrow assets without collateral if repayment happens in the same transaction
⏺ If the loan isn’t repaid, the whole transaction reverts
⏺ This post explains why flash loans are useful — and why they often appear in exploit stories

1️⃣ Core Idea — you borrow assets, use them across several steps, and repay before the transaction ends.
2️⃣ Use Cases — arbitrage, position refinancing, liquidations, and complex DeFi strategies.
3️⃣ Why No Collateral — the lender doesn’t take time risk: if repayment fails, execution fails.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — flash loans can amplify oracle attacks, thin-pool manipulation, and weak protocol logic.
5️⃣ Practical Lens — the tool isn’t “bad,” but if one burst of temporary capital can break a protocol, the design is fragile.

Final Thoughts

A flash loan is credit for one blockchain breath. Safe for the lender, but a hammer against weak protocols.

🔔 SpaceX stock falls as $60B Cursor deal closes 

‼️ SpaceX has completed its $60 billion stock-based acquisition of Anysphere, bringing the Cursor coding platform into its SpaceXAI business as SPCX shares fell during Friday trading. The closing came less than two months after SpaceX signed the merger agreement on June 16. Under its terms, the company valued Anysphere at an implied equity value of $60 billion and agreed to compensate its investors with SpaceX Class A common stock.

🔖 Cursor’s common and preferred shares outstanding immediately before the merger were automatically converted into rights to receive 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares, according to the filing.SpaceX based the exchange on the volume-weighted average closing price of its Class A shares over the seven consecutive trading days before the acquisition closed. Rather than setting one fixed share price when the agreement was signed, the structure tied the final share count to SPCX’s recent market value. 

🌐 Vested Cursor restricted stock units were separately converted into rights to receive 1,752,426 SpaceX Class A shares before applicable tax deductions. Holders will receive cash instead of fractional shares where the exchange calculation does not produce a whole share. Unvested awards will remain tied to future service and vesting requirements. According to the filing, SpaceX assumed the outstanding awards and converted them into about 29,128,326 restricted stock units linked to its Class A shares.

Kushner in Cairo: Hamas First, Netanyahu Later

Jared Kushner met Hamas leaders in Egypt before flying to Israel to see Benjamin Netanyahu. In Middle East diplomacy, this is what a hierarchy looks like when the person with guns must be persuaded before the person with an army can be briefed.

Kushner’s meeting with Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya lasted more than two hours and included Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators. 

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace’s director general for Gaza, also took part. Tony Blair was part of the wider delegation expected to continue on to meetings with Netanyahu. 

The purpose was direct. Washington wanted a personal Hamas commitment to the roadmap for Gaza, especially disarmament, before Kushner met the Israeli prime minister. 

The U.S. message was reportedly blunt: no political role for Hamas, no reconstruction and no wider Gaza political track until the group gives up its weapons and military infrastructure. 

Hamas has already agreed, in principle, to a phased disarmament plan. Heavy weapons, production sites, depots and tunnel infrastructure would be inventoried and placed under a Palestinian national committee, with international verification and a stabilization force involved. 

Israeli withdrawals are supposed to follow verified steps in that process. Hamas insists that implementation depends on Israel meeting its own obligations. 

That is the part no one says loudly enough. Hamas is being asked to trade guns for a future administration it will not run, reconstruction it will not control and Israeli withdrawals it cannot enforce. 

Israel is being asked to withdraw after Hamas disarms, but is also resisting the political plan built around that sequence.

Kushner reportedly told Hamas not to wait for Israeli elections, because Israel’s position on Gaza would not meaningfully change. That may be the clearest line of the meeting. Elections can change ministers. The U.S. message is that they will not change the terms of Palestinian surrender.

Israel’s Tzav 9 movement condemned the meeting, saying Hamas should have no legitimacy or voice after October 7. The group’s objection is instructive. The preferred peace process is one in which Hamas disarms before it speaks, and speaks only after it has disappeared.

Meanwhile, the personal commitment to disarm was reportedly delivered on the same day Israel struck two alleged militants in Gaza.

First, Hamas promises to put down its weapons.

Then Israel decides whether the promise counts.
